Two reasons it was the wrong trade. (1) The original objection — not wanting to register for anything — does not apply to ntfy: it requires no account at all, only an unguessable topic string, which is exactly why sendme.py uses it as its default backend. (2) The work would have bought a STRICTLY WORSE channel. §13.2 makes SEV1 'priority: urgent' and ntfy.go states why in its own comment: it 'is what makes a phone ring through a silent profile, which is the entire difference between a 3am alert and a 9am one'. Email has no urgency channel, so paying a gate round to lose the only signal that can wake a sleeping operator inverts the point of §13.

DECISION: §13.1 stands unamended. The push leg remains POST https://ntfy.sh/{topic} with NTFY_TOPIC from ~/.kalshi/env. No code change, no new candidate, R0 stays green. The dead man is unaffected and remains healthchecks.io, whose alarm is already email.

If email is ever wanted, the cheaper shape is ADDITIVE rather than a replacement: keep ntfy for SEV1 urgency and add email for the rest, so nothing that can wake the operator is lost.

Fixed in loop/gates.sh. Root cause reproduced and the fix verified empirically: a script that prints 61 stdout lines then one stderr diagnostic and exits 1 yields a merged stream that BEGINS with the diagnostic when stdout is block-buffered (tail -40 keeps 0 copies of it), and ENDS with it under PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 (tail -40 keeps it). Chose the ordering fix over head+tail per the bead: an interleaved head+tail of a mis-ordered stream still misleads. Three changes, all outside go/, so no gate round is consumed: (1) export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 at the top of gates.sh, restoring chronological order for every $PY step, so the tail that run() already keeps is the correct end; (2) run() now writes each step's FULL output to loop/gates-out/<step>.log and prints that path with the failure, so a truncated tail is never the only copy -- dir is rm -rf'd per run and gitignored; (3) the verdict block gained additive DISK_FREE_GB (at start and at end), LOAD and STEP_LOGS lines, addressing the bead's RELATED note that the 2026-08-11 round ran on a 99%-full volume and gates.sh reported neither. The disk line deliberately does NOT gate: a full volume is not a defect in the tree and reporting it as VERDICT: RED would send the loop hunting a phantom code bug; it is reported so a disk-exhausted round can be told apart from a rotted catalogue, which they otherwise look identical. Verdict-block changes are additive only -- the ===GATES===/VERDICT:/ADVANCE_ELIGIBLE: lines are untouched, and the only consumers are prose-parsing prompt files under loop/.
